rubric: semantic continuity, decision preservation, private-information isolation, naturalness

judgments.reason: Both preserve the single sound, safe position, and unresolved cause; text1 marks the unobserved interval more carefully and adds fewer asserted equipment details.
Both keep the cause unresolved; text1 gives a cleaner event order while text2's wording around whether to inspect or tag first is less precise.
Text1 reports only witnessed facts; text2 asserts nobody was in the pulley area during minutes when the speaker was away and could not verify that claim.

Text1 fabricates annual cycles, spring rotation, occupied slots, and candidate pressure. Text2 explicitly treats the missing deadline and consequences as unknown, although it adds some nonessential procedure detail.
Text1 preserves the unknown deadline and the player's open choice. Text2 invents a next-week deadline, immediate invalidation, one-year delay, and a temporary slot hold.
Text1 states that no authoritative deadline or downstream rule is available. Text2 invents roster locking, default abandonment, candidates, and a one-year wait.
Text1 has the NPC ask whether the player touched the cabinet area, strongly implying access to undisclosed private context. Text2 keeps the NPC focused on the missing record.
Both keep the NPC unaware; text1 is more natural and surfaces the private fact less mechanically in internal narration.
Excluded from semantic preference because one side has no model output.
